How to use this calculator

  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How day counter is calculated

Count whole calendar-day boundaries between two dates and optionally use inclusive counting. Dates are compared in UTC so daylight-saving transitions do not change the day count. Reverse endpoints are accepted and reported as an absolute difference. From March 1 to March 8 is 7 elapsed days, or 8 dates when counted inclusively. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. It counts both endpoint dates; elapsed days count the boundaries crossed. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why is inclusive count one larger?

It counts both endpoint dates; elapsed days count the boundaries crossed.

Does a leap day count?

Yes. Calendar arithmetic includes February 29 in leap years.
